title: Leflunomide for Henoch-Schonlein Purpura
off: Leflunomide for Refractory Skin Henoch-Schonlein Purpura in Children
sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University

officials.a: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University

summary: This study conducted a prospective, multicenter, one-arm clinical trial on the combination of leflunomide and steroid therapy for refractory skin Henoch-Schonlein Purpura in children on the basis of ethical principles. A one-year follow-up was conducted to evaluate the changes in the main indicators (frequency of rash recurrence) and secondary indicators (proportion of kidney damage, proportion of joint involvement, T lymphocyte subpopulations, and inflammatory factors) before and after treatment, Exploring the safety and effectiveness of leflunomide in the treatment of refractory skin type HSP in children, it is expected that leflunomide combined with conventional treatment can improve the remission rate of HSP children's skin purpura and reduce HSP recurrence. The research results are expected to bring new treatment methods and strategies for this group of patients.

arms.l: Administration of Leflunomide in refractory skin Henoch-Schonlein purpura
arms.d: Rashes are dense and large in area, often treated with antibiotics, antihistamines, calcium supplements, and glucocorticoids (2 mg/kg/d) for 5 days. The rash does not subside or new rash still appears, and it frequently repeats more than 3 times during hospitalization.
